lessons.title: In Order to & Planning to: The Purposive Converb (-хаар/-хээр)

lessons.primaryPurpose: Introduce the purposive converb suffix (-хаар4 / -хээр / -хоор / -хөөр) indicating goal/purpose ('in order to') and immediate planned intention ('planning to / about to do' when paired with байна/болох).
lessons.communicativeOutcome: State purpose of actions: 'Би монгол хэл сурахаар ирсэн' (I came to learn Mongolian), 'Бид маргааш хөдөө явахаар төлөвлөж байна' (We are planning to go to the countryside tomorrow).
lessons.audioPurpose: Model quadruple vowel harmony in purposive suffix (-хаар, -хээр, -хоор, -хөөр).

grammarOverview.summary: Introduce the purposive converb suffix (-хаар4 / -хээр / -хоор / -хөөр) indicating goal/purpose ('in order to') and immediate planned intention ('planning to / about to do' when paired with байна/болох).

lessons.title: They Said That: Reported Speech with Гэж & Гэсэн
lessons.cyrillicTitle: Relay messages and third-party statements: 'Багш маргааш хичээлгүй гэж хэлсэн' (The teacher said there is no class tomorrow), 'Болд ирнэ гэсэн' (Bold said he would come).
lessons.primaryPurpose: Introduce direct and indirect quotation structures using the quotative particle гэж + speech verbs (хэлэх, асуух, ярих) and colloquial evidential particle гэсэн ('they said that / apparently').
lessons.communicativeOutcome: Relay messages and third-party statements: 'Багш маргааш хичээлгүй гэж хэлсэн' (The teacher said there is no class tomorrow), 'Болд ирнэ гэсэн' (Bold said he would come).

lessons.title: It Has Come to Pass: The Resultative Past Tense (-жээ/-чээ)
lessons.cyrillicTitle: Celebrate accomplishments and note completed changes: 'Манай хүү том болжээ' (Our son has grown so big!), 'Шинэ жил иржээ' (The New Year has arrived!).
lessons.primaryPurpose: Introduce the resultative past/evidential tense suffix (-жээ / -чээ) indicating completed actions whose ongoing results or realization have just become evident, frequently used in milestone appraisals, toasts, and discovery.
lessons.communicativeOutcome: Celebrate accomplishments and note completed changes: 'Манай хүү том болжээ' (Our son has grown so big!), 'Шинэ жил иржээ' (The New Year has arrived!).
lessons.audioPurpose: Model phonotactic distribution of -жээ (after vowels and voiced consonants) vs -чээ (after voiceless consonants).

grammarOverview.summary: Introduce the resultative past/evidential tense suffix (-жээ / -чээ) indicating completed actions whose ongoing results or realization have just become evident, frequently used in milestone appraisals, toasts, and discovery.

lessons.title: The City Where I Was Born: Relative Clause Participles (-сан, -даг, -х)
lessons.cyrillicTitle: Form complex modifier clauses describing people, places, and events: 'Миний төрсөн хот' (The city where I was born), 'Бидний очдог газар' (The place we usually go), 'Миний хараахан хийгээгүй ажил' (Work I haven't done yet).
lessons.primaryPurpose: Introduce the foundational Mongolian relative clause architecture using pre-nominal verbal participles: past perfective (-сан4), habitual present (-даг4), and prospective future (-х), along with participle negation (-аагүй4).
lessons.communicativeOutcome: Form complex modifier clauses describing people, places, and events: 'Миний төрсөн хот' (The city where I was born), 'Бидний очдог газар' (The place we usually go), 'Миний хараахан хийгээгүй ажил' (Work I haven't done yet).
lessons.audioPurpose: Model seamless prosodic juncture between modifying clause and head noun.

grammarOverview.summary: Introduce the foundational Mongolian relative clause architecture using pre-nominal verbal participles: past perfective (-сан4), habitual present (-даг4), and prospective future (-х), along with participle negation (-аагүй4).
